name: Semaglutide
route_note: subcutaneous injection once weekly (Ozempic, Wegovy) or oral tablet once daily taken fasting with absorption enhancer SNAC (Rybelsus)

discovery.note: Successor to liraglutide with Aib8 substitution for DPP-4 resistance and a C18 fatty diacid linker for strong albumin binding, giving a weekly half-life. Year is the priority date of Novo Nordisk's patent application on acylated GLP-1 compounds (WO 2006/097537); the discovery was published by Lau et al. in J. Med. Chem. 2015.

tagline: Once-weekly GLP-1 drug for diabetes and obesity that reshaped medicine and markets
summary: Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist given weekly by injection or daily as a tablet. It lowers glucose and produces about 15% average weight loss at obesity doses, reduces cardiovascular events and kidney disease progression, and became one of the best-selling medicines in the world.
mechanism: Semaglutide activates the GLP-1 receptor, increasing glucose-dependent insulin secretion, lowering glucagon and slowing gastric emptying. An alpha-aminoisobutyric acid at position 8 blocks DPP-4 cleavage and an octadecanedioic fatty diacid chain binds albumin strongly, giving a half-life of about one week.
Through brain GLP-1 receptors in the hypothalamus and hindbrain the drug also reduces appetite and food intake, and it slows gastric emptying; together these effects produce weight loss.

The oral tablet is co-formulated with sodium N-[8-(2-hydroxybenzoyl)amino]caprylate (SNAC), which locally raises gastric pH and aids absorption across the stomach lining; bioavailability is still only about 1%.
uses: Reduction of major cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes with CVD (Ozempic) and in obesity with CVD (Wegovy)
Chronic weight management in obesity or overweight with comorbidity (Wegovy, adults and adolescents 12+)
Reducing kidney disease progression in type 2 diabetes with CKD (Ozempic)

history.title: SUSTAIN-6
history.detail: Weekly semaglutide reduces major cardiovascular events by 26% versus placebo in type 2 diabetes.

history.title: First oral GLP-1
history.detail: FDA approves Rybelsus in September 2019, the first oral GLP-1 receptor agonist.

history.title: Wegovy for obesity
history.detail: After STEP 1 shows about 15% mean weight loss, FDA approves Wegovy 2.4 mg in June 2021.

history.title: Shortages and compounding
history.detail: Demand outstrips supply; FDA lists semaglutide in shortage, allowing compounded versions until early 2025.

history.title: SELECT
history.detail: SELECT shows a 20% reduction in major cardiovascular events in adults with obesity and CVD without diabetes.

history.title: Cardiovascular label and FLOW
history.detail: FDA adds a cardiovascular indication to Wegovy (March); FLOW shows reduced kidney outcomes in diabetic CKD.

history.title: Kidney and MASH indications
history.detail: FDA approves Ozempic to reduce kidney disease progression (January) and Wegovy for MASH with fibrosis (August); WHO adds GLP-1 agonists to the Essential Medicines List.

history.title: Patent expiry in several countries
history.detail: The core semaglutide patent expires in India and Brazil in March 2026 and has lapsed in Canada; several Indian companies launch generic versions on 21 March 2026.

pk.metabolism: proteolysis of the peptide backbone and beta-oxidation of the fatty-acid side chain

safety.boxed_warning: Risk of thyroid C-cell tumours: caused C-cell tumours in rodents; contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

facts: Rybelsus was the first oral GLP-1 receptor agonist (2019).
Semaglutide sales made Novo Nordisk Europe's most valuable listed company for a period in 2023–2024.
The 2025 WHO Essential Medicines List added GLP-1 receptor agonists including semaglutide.

references.title: Business Today: India semaglutide market opens post patent expiry (March 2026)
